page: Microsoft Azure DC16s_v3 is a memory-optimized virtual machine from the DCSv3 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 16 dedicated physical cores (16 vCPUs) powered by an Intel Xeon 8370C x86_64 processor operating at 2.8 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 128.0 GB of system memory, providing a 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It lacks local storage and integrated GPUs, but it is Premium Storage capable for external disk attachments.

Benchmark data positions this server in the average tier across most compute and memory operations. The Intel Xeon processor delivers a single-core Geekbench score of 1674.0 and a multi-core score of 13843.0, alongside a Passmark CPU score of 30808.33. Memory performance is characterized by a read-only small block cached bandwidth of 1687.72 GB/sec and a large block uncached write bandwidth of 60.51 GB/sec. Notably, the server shows strong performance in Geekbench image processing at 13806.0 and small-model LLM text generation at 316.58 tokens/sec for a 135M model.

A key tradeoff is the lack of local storage and GPU acceleration, which limits its utility for heavy local disk I/O or parallel computing tasks. Furthermore, LLM inference performance drops significantly on larger models, with prompt processing for a 70B model yielding a weak score of 6.61 tokens/sec. Given its 128.0 GB memory capacity and dedicated 16-core CPU allocation, this server is appropriate for memory-intensive workloads, database operations, software compilation, and moderate web serving.
